question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Paris, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

notes.anthropic: France's biggest home-grown mega-gallery, with global outposts; launched Murakami, Sophie Calle, JR and Kaws in Europe and anchors the Marais scene.
notes.openai: Paris-founded international powerhouse known for a large, globally visible programme and major art-fair presence.

galleries.name: Thaddaeus Ropac
galleries.address_hint: 7 rue Debelleyme (plus a vast space in Pantin)

notes.anthropic: Blue-chip programme (Baselitz, Kiefer, Rauschenberg estate, Warhol) split between an intimate Marais townhouse and a museum-scale Pantin hangar.
notes.openai: A leading European gallery representing major postwar and contemporary artists across ambitious Paris exhibitions.

galleries.name: Gagosian
galleries.address_hint: 4 rue de Ponthieu (plus 9 rue de Castiglione)

notes.anthropic: Two Paris spaces from the world's most powerful dealer, driving the 8th arrondissement's revival around Art Basel Paris.
notes.openai: The Paris arm of the global mega-gallery, with exceptional blue-chip artists, market power and institutional reach.

notes.anthropic: Opened 2019 and immediately central to Paris's internationalisation; shows Kerry James Marshall, Wolfgang Tillmans, Raymond Pettibon, Njideka Akunyili Crosby.
notes.openai: The Paris branch of a top-tier global gallery with a museum-calibre programme and powerful secondary market.

notes.anthropic: Paris arm of the legendary New York dealer; Gerhard Richter, Steve McQueen, Tacita Dean, William Kentridge, Annette Messager.
notes.openai: Historically crucial for introducing major European conceptual artists to international audiences and vice versa.

notes.anthropic: Its 2023 Paris flagship brought Louise Bourgeois, Mark Bradford, Pipilotti Rist and a major estate programme to the Golden Triangle.
notes.openai: A global mega-gallery whose substantial Paris space presents leading living artists and major estates.

notes.anthropic: Since 1980 a benchmark for conceptual and international rigour: Gonzalez-Foerster, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Mona Hatoum, Wolfgang Tillmans, Danh Vo.
notes.openai: A defining Paris gallery for conceptually rigorous international art, with sustained institutional influence.

notes.anthropic: International network gallery mixing Picasso estate scholarship with a strong figurative-painting roster.
notes.openai: A highly international gallery spanning canonical postwar figures, established contemporaries and younger painters.

galleries.name: Templon
galleries.address_hint: 30 rue Beaubourg / 28 rue du Grenier Saint-Lazare

notes.anthropic: Founded 1966, the historic Paris gallery for American and European painting; Kehinde Wiley, Chiharu Shiota, Omar Ba, Jitish Kallat.
notes.openai: A pillar of the Paris scene since 1966, with deep ties to American, European and French contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: London powerhouse's 2023 Paris space; Tracey Emin, Julie Mehretu, Theaster Gates and a strong estates programme.
notes.openai: The prominent London gallery's permanent Paris space brings a globally recognised roster to the city.

galleries.name: Galerie Max Hetzler
galleries.address_hint: 57 rue du Temple (and 46 rue Vieille du Temple)

notes.anthropic: Berlin dealer's Paris spaces; Albert Oehlen, Bridget Riley, Camille Henrot, Rebecca Warren, top-tier fair presence.

notes.anthropic: Historic house with a publishing arm; Jaume Plensa, Kiki Smith, Barthélémy Toguo, plus major estates (Tàpies, Bacon prints).

galleries.name: Galerie Nathalie Obadia

notes.anthropic: Two Marais spaces and Brussels; Fiona Rae, Josep Grau-Garriga estate, Andres Serrano, Youssef Nabil, Laure Prouvost.

notes.anthropic: San Gimignano-born international gallery; Kader Attia, JR, Anish Kapoor, Pascale Marthine Tayou, with a strong Global South emphasis.
